arabic-tah.context: Arabic letter tah (ط): a flat closed loop lying on the line with a tall straight stroke rising from its left end. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-zah.context: Arabic letter zah (ظ): the tah shape of a flat loop and tall upright stroke, with one dot above the loop. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-ghayn.context: Arabic letter ghayn (غ): a small open c shaped head on a large open curve that sweeps down and around below the line, with one dot above. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-fa.context: Arabic letter fa (ف): a small round loop on the right end of a long flat stroke that curls up at the left, with one dot above the loop. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-qaf.context: Arabic letter qaf (ق): a small round loop on top of a deep round bowl sweeping below the line, with two dots above. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-kaf.context: Arabic letter kaf (ك): a tall upright stroke on the left joined to a flat base that curls up at the right, with a small s like squiggle inside. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-lam.context: Arabic letter lam (ل): a tall straight stroke that curves at its foot into a deep round bowl rising back up on the left. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-mim.context: Arabic letter mim (م): a small closed round loop on the line with a straight tail dropping down beneath it. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-nun.context: Arabic letter nun (ن): a deep round open bowl like a cup with one dot above its centre. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-heh.context: Arabic letter heh (ه): a small rounded teardrop loop with a smaller loop folded inside it. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-waw.context: Arabic letter waw (و): a small round head loop with a tail curving down and to the left below the line. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-ya.context: Arabic letter ya (ي): a small curl at the top right dropping into a wide bowl that sweeps back to the right under the line, with two dots below. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-alif-maqsura.context: Arabic letter alif maqsura (ى): the ya shape of a top curl and wide sweeping bowl with no dots. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-hamza.context: Arabic hamza (ء): a small standalone hooked mark like a backwards c whose lower end flicks out into a short diagonal tail. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-ta-marbuta.context: Arabic ta marbuta (ة): a small closed round loop like heh with two dots side by side above it. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-lam-alif.context: Arabic lam alif ligature (لا): two tall strokes crossing in a V that join at a small loop at the base. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-peh.context: Arabic script letter peh (Persian, Urdu) (پ): the shallow canoe shaped bowl with three dots in a triangle below it. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-tcheh.context: Arabic script letter tcheh (Persian, Urdu) (چ): the folded top stroke and deep reversed C sweep of jim with three dots inside the curve. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-jeh.context: Arabic script letter jeh (Persian) (ژ): the comma like ra stroke with three dots in a triangle above it. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

arabic-gaf.context: Arabic script letter gaf (Persian, Urdu) (گ): a tall slanted stroke on the left joined to a flat base that curls up at the right, with a second short slanted bar parallel above the top. Used for Arabic, Persian and Urdu alphabet charts, language learning, calligraphy practice and type samples.

hangul-giyeok.context: Hangul consonant giyeok (ㄱ): a horizontal stroke across the top that turns sharply down at the right end into a vertical stroke. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-digeut.context: Hangul consonant digeut (ㄷ): a squared C of a top bar, a left upright and a bottom bar that reaches further right than the top. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-rieul.context: Hangul consonant rieul (ㄹ): three horizontal strokes joined by alternating right and left uprights, like a squared S. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-bieup.context: Hangul consonant bieup (ㅂ): two vertical stems joined by a middle crossbar and a closed bottom bar, like an open topped box with a shelf. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-jieut.context: Hangul consonant jieut (ㅈ): a horizontal top bar with an upside down V hanging from its centre. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-chieut.context: Hangul consonant chieut (ㅊ): the jieut shape of a top bar over an upside down V, with a short tick stroke above the bar. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-kieuk.context: Hangul consonant kieuk (ㅋ): the giyeok right angle with an extra short horizontal stroke through its middle. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-pieup.context: Hangul consonant pieup (ㅍ): a top bar and a longer bottom bar joined by two short vertical stems, like a small stool. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-hieut.context: Hangul consonant hieut (ㅎ): a short tick on top of a horizontal bar, sitting above a small circle. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ssanggiyeok.context: Hangul double consonant ssanggiyeok (ㄲ): two small giyeok right angles side by side. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ssangdigeut.context: Hangul double consonant ssangdigeut (ㄸ): two small squared C digeut shapes side by side. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ssangbieup.context: Hangul double consonant ssangbieup (ㅃ): two small bieup boxes with crossbars side by side. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ssangsiot.context: Hangul double consonant ssangsiot (ㅆ): two small upside down V shapes like tiny tents side by side. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ssangjieut.context: Hangul double consonant ssangjieut (ㅉ): two small jieut shapes, each a top bar over an upside down V, side by side. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-a.context: Hangul vowel a (ㅏ): a tall vertical stroke with one short horizontal tick sticking out to the right at mid height. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ya.context: Hangul vowel ya (ㅑ): a tall vertical stroke with two short horizontal ticks sticking out to the right. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-eo.context: Hangul vowel eo (ㅓ): a tall vertical stroke with one short horizontal tick sticking out to the left at mid height. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-yeo.context: Hangul vowel yeo (ㅕ): a tall vertical stroke with two short horizontal ticks sticking out to the left. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-yo.context: Hangul vowel yo (ㅛ): a long horizontal base bar with two short vertical ticks standing on it. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ae.context: Hangul vowel ae (ㅐ): two tall vertical strokes side by side with one short tick running from the left stroke toward the right one. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-e.context: Hangul vowel e (ㅔ): two tall vertical strokes side by side with one short tick sticking out to the left of the left stroke. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-yae.context: Hangul vowel yae (ㅒ): two tall vertical strokes side by side with two short ticks running from the left stroke toward the right one. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ye.context: Hangul vowel ye (ㅖ): two tall vertical strokes side by side with two short ticks sticking out to the left of the left stroke. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-wa.context: Hangul vowel wa (ㅘ): a short upright tick standing on a horizontal bar at the lower left, beside a tall vertical with a tick to the right. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-wae.context: Hangul vowel wae (ㅙ): a short upright tick on a horizontal bar at the lower left, beside two tall verticals with a tick between them. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-oe.context: Hangul vowel oe (ㅚ): a short upright tick standing on a horizontal bar at the lower left, beside a plain tall vertical stroke. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-wo.context: Hangul vowel wo (ㅝ): a horizontal bar with a short stem dropping below it at the lower left, beside a tall vertical with a tick to the left. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-we.context: Hangul vowel we (ㅞ): a horizontal bar with a short stem dropping below it, beside two tall verticals with a tick out to the left. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-wi.context: Hangul vowel wi (ㅟ): a horizontal bar with a short stem dropping below it at the lower left, beside a plain tall vertical stroke. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hangul-ui.context: Hangul vowel ui (ㅢ): a plain horizontal bar at the lower left beside a plain tall vertical stroke on the right. Used for Korean alphabet charts, language learning, keyboards and type samples.

hiragana-i.context: Hiragana i (い): two short near vertical strokes side by side, the left one longer with a small hook at its foot. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-u.context: Hiragana u (う): a short dash on top above a stroke that arcs right and sweeps down into a hook to the lower left. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-e.context: Hiragana e (え): a short dash on top above a zigzag that runs right, cuts diagonally down left, then ends in a long flat tail to the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-o.context: Hiragana o (お): a horizontal bar crossed by a vertical stroke that loops into a round belly on the right, with a small dash at the upper right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ka.context: Hiragana ka (か): an angular stroke like a 7 with a hooked foot crossed by a slanted downstroke, plus a separate short dash at the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ki.context: Hiragana ki (き): two horizontal bars crossed by a slanted stroke, with a separate open curve at the bottom. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ke.context: Hiragana ke (け): a tall curved upright on the left, and on the right a horizontal bar crossed by a long stroke curving down to the left. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ko.context: Hiragana ko (こ): two short curved horizontal strokes stacked, the top one ending in a small hook and the bottom one curving up at the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-sa.context: Hiragana sa (さ): a horizontal bar crossed by a slanted stroke, above a separate open curve like a backwards c. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-shi.context: Hiragana shi (し): a single long stroke that drops straight down and curves up to the right at the bottom like a hook. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-su.context: Hiragana su (す): a horizontal bar crossed by a vertical stroke that makes a small loop before dropping into a tail. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-se.context: Hiragana se (せ): a long horizontal bar crossed by a short right upright and a longer left upright that curves into a flat base. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-so.context: Hiragana so (そ): a zigzag of a short dash, a diagonal, a long horizontal and a curved tail sweeping down and back to the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ta.context: Hiragana ta (た): a cross shaped stroke on the left beside two short horizontal strokes stacked on the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-chi.context: Hiragana chi (ち): a horizontal bar crossed by a slanted stroke that bends into a rounded bowl opening to the left, like a 5. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-tsu.context: Hiragana tsu (つ): a single wide arch that starts flat on the left, curves over at the right and sweeps down into a hook to the lower left. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-te.context: Hiragana te (て): a horizontal stroke that folds back at the right end and curves down into a long c shape. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-to.context: Hiragana to (と): a short slanted stroke above a second stroke that curves down and back to the right into a flat base. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-na.context: Hiragana na (な): a cross shaped stroke with a short dash on the right, above a small loop at the lower right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ni.context: Hiragana ni (に): a tall curved upright on the left beside two short horizontal strokes stacked on the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-nu.context: Hiragana nu (ぬ): two crossing diagonal strokes forming an overlapping loop that ends in a small round curl at the lower right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ne.context: Hiragana ne (ね): a tall vertical stroke on the left crossed by a zigzag that loops around to the right and ends in a small curl. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-no.context: Hiragana no (の): a single spiral stroke starting at the centre that curves over the top and around, like a cursive @. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ha.context: Hiragana ha (は): a tall upright on the left, and on the right a horizontal bar crossed by a stroke ending in a small loop. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-hi.context: Hiragana hi (ひ): a single stroke that starts with a short flick, dips into a deep round bowl and rises with a flick at the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-fu.context: Hiragana fu (ふ): four small separate strokes: a top curve, a central hooked bowl and a dot on each side. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-he.context: Hiragana he (へ): a single stroke rising to a short peak on the left and descending in a longer gentle slope to the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ho.context: Hiragana ho (ほ): a tall upright on the left, and on the right two horizontal bars crossed by a stroke ending in a small loop. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-ma.context: Hiragana ma (ま): two horizontal bars crossed by a vertical stroke that ends in a small loop at the bottom. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.

hiragana-mi.context: Hiragana mi (み): a stroke that zigzags into a loop at the lower left and sweeps right, crossed by a short slanted stroke at the right. Used for Japanese kana charts, language learning, flashcards and type samples.
